req1: ## Requirement 1 — A briefing a health office can send
User story: As a Dinkes officer, I want a short text with this window's priority districts, so that I can send it to puskesmas heads on WhatsApp or print it for the morning meeting.

1.1. WHEN the user opens the briefing, THE SYSTEM SHALL produce, in the current language (Bahasa Indonesia or English), a plain-text briefing with the region, the window dates, the mode (live or replay as hindsight), up to five ranked districts with their mean change in visits and its 95% range, the haze and fire-haze days, the profile, the mapped puskesmas count, the incomplete districts, the data times, any failed source, the method source, every method limit, and a line that it is not medical advice.
1.2. THE SYSTEM SHALL generate the briefing text in the engine, so that the web app (WebAssembly) and the MCP tool (native CLI) return byte-identical text for identical input.
1.3. WHEN no district with complete data has a haze day in the window, THE SYSTEM SHALL say so instead of listing districts.
1.4. THE SYSTEM SHALL offer copy, share to WhatsApp, download as .txt, and print, without sending the text anywhere by itself.
1.5. IF the metadata given to the engine is malformed (control characters, a non-https link, an out-of-range count), THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse it with a clear error instead of writing a briefing.

rules: 1. Real data only. The product never shows mock or made-up data. Every layer and every number names its source and the time it refers to.
2. Ranges, not single numbers. Every estimate shows its 95% interval next to the point value, plus the study it comes from.

3. Say the limits on screen. The method comes from one study of six puskesmas in Central Kalimantan (Phung et al. 2025). The effect was clear in Pulang Pisau and absent in Palangka Raya city. The app says so where the numbers appear.
4. Never present stale data as current. If a source fails or is old, the UI shows which source and how old, and the outlook is marked incomplete.
5. Decision support, not diagnosis. The app estimates load on clinics; it does not give medical advice to individuals.

mcp.text:
Sootsayer haze briefing: Kalimantan, 14–18 Oct 2026 for the district health office
Replay (hindsight): archived model data, not the forecast issued on that day

Priority for posko and oxygen houses
Expected change in puskesmas respiratory visits, mean over 5 days, with 95% range:
1. Pulang Pisau: +88% (+14% … +211%); 5 haze days, 5 with local fires, regency profile, 1 mapped puskesmas
2. Barito Selatan: +87% (+17% … +199%); 5 haze days, 4 with local fires, regency profile, 4 mapped puskesmas
3. Kapuas: +87% (+17% … +199%); 5 haze days, 4 with local fires, regency profile, 5 mapped puskesmas
4. Hulu Sungai Utara: +86% (+21% … +188%); 5 haze days, 3 with local fires, regency profile, 8 mapped puskesmas
5. Katingan: +81% (+13% … +191%); 5 haze days, 5 with local fires, regency profile, 0 mapped puskesmas

Data sources:
• Copernicus CAMS + NASA FIRMS: 2026-11-11T10:49:53Z
Method: Phung et al. 2025, Int J Epidemiol, doi:10.1093/ije/dyaf169 (Table 4, main model).
Method limits:
• One study: six puskesmas in Palangka Raya and Pulang Pisau, 2015-2019.
• The effect was clear in Pulang Pisau (kabupaten) and absent in Palangka Raya city (kota); the authors call the overall result inconclusive.
• Outside Central Kalimantan the study's estimates are applied by analogy: other Kalimantan provinces and Sumatra were not part of the study.
• Relative risks are cumulative over lag 0-5 days and are applied as daily multipliers, which is exact only for sustained haze.
• Smoke values are model estimates (CAMS, about 45 km grid), not station measurements.
This estimates clinic load for planning. It is not medical advice for individuals.
Details: https://sootsayer.vercel.app/?region=kalimantan&mode=replay&date=2026-10-14
